input: A label-source split for a supernova catalog reads archived public name-server pages. For one SN Ia (SN 2023pjg) the only classification report was sent by the account ZTF_Bot1 and its Classifier/s field reads 'C. Fremling, D. Neill, Y. Sharma on behalf of the SEDM Team (Caltech) and the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) based on SNIascore'. The methods paper states that SNIascore is a recurrent neural network that classifies SNe Ia from low-resolution spectra and reports them without human interaction. Because three named people appear in the classifier field, the split proposes to count this label as a measured human classification. Rule.

The same split finds, for SN 2023hdf (catalog type SN Ia), a latest classification report sent by the account ZTF_Bot1 whose Classifier/s field reads 'J. Johansson, W. Meynardie, M. Chu, C. Fremling (Caltech) on behalf of the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF)', with no automated-classifier name in that field, and a public spectrum dated before the report. A reviewer proposes to move the label to model annotation because the sending account is a bot. Dispose.

A calibration item set for transient classification contains SN 2019odp, typed SN Ib in the catalog. A 2020 survey paper read by the panel labels this object in a figure panel as '2019odp (Ic−BL, z=0.014)'. The item builder argues refusal 14 does not apply because the class in the paper disagrees with the catalog label, so the item's answer is not in the text. Every candidate subject's published knowledge cutoff is in 2025 or 2026. Rule.

The same paper lists SN2019sxd (ZTF19acdsqir) in its table of non-name-server classifications with an en dash in the Classification column, which the table note defines as retaining the existing name-server classification, and a note 'Added redshift from NED'. No class token for this object appears anywhere in the paper. The item would use a neutral identifier, withhold all seed text from every arm, and is designated calibration only with contamination FAIL disclosed; the exposure ruling for that use is written. A reviewer proposes to refuse it under the answer-in-own-source rule because the object is named in the paper. Dispose.
